issues.what: Every unsupervised fit (RV z-scoring, GMM, HMM, jump centroids + lambda, BOCPD standardisation, FFD d*) is estimated once on the first IS half (489 of 1,026 IS sessions) and then applied to all bars, including the fit window's own bars. The design's binding leakage control for regime-states says parameters and z-scoring statistics are 'estimated on IS training-fold bars only, refit per fold'. For the harness splitter this means blocks 0-4 are 100% inside the fit window and block 5 is 72% inside: the 35 model-derived columns are in-sample there and out-of-sample for blocks 6-11. Label-free, so no outcome can leak, and the study discloses the in-sample effect, but it does not spell out that Judge 2's two-halves stability check (2021-10..2023-09 vs 2023-10..2025-12) for these columns compares an in-sample half with an out-of-sample half, nor that the truncation check is blind to it.

issues.what: d* for the FFD is chosen on the fit window rather than 'on IS bars' as the design method specifies. Disclosed in the caveats, but the README's column table describes the column as 'chosen by ADF' without saying the shipped series fails the ADF over IS.

result.verified: Lens = arithmetic, controls, multiplicity. This is a feature-building study that makes no gate claim, proposes no candidate and has ledger_families = []; the control percentile / permutation p / kept-n floors / top-1%-removed / CPCV / PBO / SPA items of the lens are therefore not required and the study says so explicitly (FINDINGS.md:3, :88-90). Confirmed: the ledger (892 rows in ledger/trials.jsonl) contains no row mentioning ext_features or features_ext; build_ext.py reads features.parquet with columns [setup_i, dir_sign, n_choch_since_bos] only (line 58) and write_docs.py uses harness.load(tf).n for the row count only (line 13), so no label column was read. Reproduced from the output files and data (scratchpad script checkA.py): rows 5,326 / 1,012; 61 columns (+ setup_i); L1 units 5,266 / 1,002 via H.load; bars 443,826 / 88,771; fit window 182,557 bars / 489 sessions (1m) and 36,514 / 489 (5m); IS SETUPs 4,502 / 832, OOS 824 / 180; setup_i keys identical to the base table; ext_features.parquet == ext_features_all.parquet. Coverage dict identical to findings.json on both timeframes; min 0.9812 / 0.9427, median 1.0; the four columns below 0.99 reproduce and their arithmetic checks: CSW coverage = share(session_bar >= 2) exactly (0.9812 / 0.9427), FFD coverage = share(setup_i >= 502) exactly (0.997 / 0.9911). HMM tables: findings.json state means == ext_fit_report.json; states ordered ascending by range_atr as stated; stationary distribution and dwell recomputed from the reported transition matrices agree to the 4-dp rounding (e.g. 0.1324 vs 0.1327; 46.1 vs 46.0); filter-check numbers match the logs. Full independent rebuild of the 5-minute table from scratchpad copies of build_ext.py + ext_lib.py: bit-identical to the published ext_features_all.parquet (max |diff| 0 over all 62 columns), identical HMM/GMM state means, lambda* (32 / 16) and d*. ADF re-run for minute log close: d=0.2 fit ADF -5.347 pass, all-IS -2.538 fail (crit -2.862); d=0.3 all-IS -4.687 pass -> d*(fit) 0.2, d*(IS) 0.3 as reported, window lengths 497 (d=0.2) / 503 (d=0.1) reproduced from ffd_weights. Code walk of every kernel in ext_lib.py / build_ext.py: FFD by full convolution truncated to len(y) (bars <= t), rolling z over [t-win+1, t], BSADF regressions over bars s..k, CUSUM forward filter with counts in (t-60, t], CSW over the session's bars s0..k, BOCPD forward recursion, rv_logvol_rel20 median over k-20..k-1 (shift(1)), same-session windows cut at s0, HMM forward filter (validated against hmmlearn at the last bar of a 600-bar prefix and by log-likelihood to 1e-11), jump online prefix DP, novelty MASS with library close[0..k-m-1] and query ending at k, window summaries over bars <= k: all as-of.
